differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Aerospike uses a hybrid memory architecture, storing indexes in RAM and data on SSDs for cost-effective scalability and persistence.
differences.rightDesc: Redis primarily stores data structures in RAM. Persistence is achieved via snapshots (RDB) or append-only files (AOF), with optional disk offloading.

differences.title: 2. CONSISTENCY
differences.leftDesc: Aerospike offers strong consistency with tunable per-request read/write consistency levels, ensuring data integrity across nodes.
differences.rightDesc: Redis typically offers eventual consistency in clustered setups. Single-node Redis is strongly consistent but lacks high availability.

differences.title: 3. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Aerospike scales horizontally via its distributed architecture, automatically rebalancing data and client connections across nodes.
differences.rightDesc: Redis scales horizontally using client-side sharding or Redis Cluster, which partitions data across multiple instances.

differences.title: 4. SECONDARY INDEXES
differences.leftDesc: Aerospike supports efficient secondary indexes directly within the database, allowing complex queries on non-key fields.
differences.rightDesc: Redis has limited support for secondary indexes, often requiring client-side logic or Lua scripting for complex lookups.

differences.title: 5. DATA TYPES
differences.leftDesc: Aerospike supports complex data types like lists, maps, sets, and geo-spatial types, suitable for diverse application needs.
differences.rightDesc: Redis excels with a variety of built-in data structures including strings, lists, sets, sorted sets, hashes, and bitmaps.

differences.title: 6. OPERATIONAL MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Aerospike provides robust multi-datacenter replication with active-active capabilities, ensuring high availability and disaster recovery.
differences.rightDesc: Redis primarily uses primary-replica replication. Sentinel manages failover, while Cluster handles data distribution and availability.

differences.title: 7. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Aerospike is engineered for predictable, low-latency reads and writes, especially with large datasets and SSDs.
differences.rightDesc: Redis offers extremely high throughput for in-memory operations, making it ideal for caching and real-time use cases.
